newsitem.title: UK: Crude oil tankers - West Africa weak, others flat.
newsitem.headline: Crude oil tankers - West Africa weak, others flat.

text.p: Crude oil tanker rates from West Africa were weaker on Thursday while rates in other parts of the world were flat, ship brokers said.
"West Africa is dead - it has lost its buzz," one player said, citing Agip's fixture of the million barrel Zante Corcovado, an older ship, to Italy at a lacklustre W84. "That is a serious drop."
Transatlantic voyages from West Africa, for similar size ships were worth W90-95, compared to last week's W97.5 amid limited enquiries for tonnage.
"It could go soon below 90," one broker said.
Continued bad weather in the North Sea, which has already caused some limited loading delays, was not expected to boost rates immediately because of the surplus tonnage available.
But brokers said that a continuation could boost rates. Brokers noted enquiries for arbitrage vessels to move transatlantic, which could further support this market.
Middle eastern markets were quiet, following fixtures of ULCCs earlier in the week. The 275,000 tonne Golar Edinburgh was fixed to Japan at W62.5 - a higher rate than previous fixtures.
Dealers said this was a modern ship, and these are currently in relatively short supply for the end of the month.
They assessed the market a couple of points lower.
Rates for 25,000 tonne fuel oil cargoes in northwest Europe were steady to strong.
Russian material continues to leak out of the Baltics and this has provided a little support to the market.
